subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw add manifest-declared install-time config intent for third-party plugins, and what allowed paths, confirmation, conflict/array behavior, provenance, and uninstall guidance must it require?
rationale: This changes plugin install from enabling package metadata to letting package metadata mutate persisted user configuration, which crosses security, upgrade-safety, and product boundaries that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Define Guarded Config Intent
options.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates pending config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and classifies or blocks sensitive paths before writing.

options.title: Keep Manual Setup For Now
options.body: Reject manifest-driven writes and keep plugins using docs, setup flows, provider auth, or explicit `openclaw config patch` commands until a safer contract is designed.

options.title: Gate Through ClawHub Trust
options.body: Require ClawHub/package trust metadata or plugin setup approval to carry install-time config requests before core accepts them.

recommendation.title: Define Guarded Config Intent
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates pending config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and classifies or blocks sensitive paths before writing.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the clearest current product/security framing on this issue and show recent ownership signals in the manifest/install surfaces.
